 Masters invite would nice Christmas present this year: McNealy
 By
 Associated Press , 
 By
 Associated Press 
     Published November 18, 2026 02:47 PM 
 Twitter 
 Email
 How will the weather impact the RSM Classic? 
 Golf Channel's Rex Hoggard gave the lastest update on the weather from this week's RSM Classic. 
 NAPLES, Fla. — Keith Mitchell enjoys playing the RSM Classic at Sea Island because it’s a home game now that he lives in the Georgia coastal community. Even better is when he doesn’t have to cope with the pressure that comes with the final tournament of the PGA Tour season. 
 Mitchell took care of that with a runner-up finish in Japan, and a top 10 in Mexico. He is No. 52 in the FedEx Cup Fall, making him a lock for $20 million signature events at Pebble Beach and Riviera.
 “I still want to play well this week,” Mitchell said Tuesday. “It’s a little bit easier without the extra added pressure.”
 That falls to so many others.
 The RSM Classic is the final tournament for players to finish among the top 100 in the FedEx Cup to secure full cards for 2027, a transition year to the new model of two tiers. Everyone from No. 93 (Kevin Roy) to No. 100 (Christiaan Bezuidenhout) is at Sea Island.
 Right behind is Billy Horschel, who fell out of the top 100 last week.
 That’s not the only bubble. The top 60 are assured two signature events to start next year, at Pebble and Riviera. Max Homa looked to be in good shape, until different winners and big moves bumped him out, and then he played his way back to No. 60 going into Sea Island.
 Ben Kohles, who only a month ago was trying to keep his card, suddenly is No. 61 after finishing runner-up in the Austin Championship on Monday.
 The other bubble is a little more complicated. The top 50 in the world ranking at the end of the year get into the Masters. Some players might not have another chance this year. Others might go to Australia or pull a Ryan Gerard and fly to Mauritius to try to lock up top-50 status.
 Rickie Fowler is not in the Masters field and is sitting at No. 49. He has played only once in the last three months and is not at the RSM Classic. Fowler received a spot in the Hero World Challenge, overlooked news because of the return of Tiger Woods. 
 Harris English is at No. 47 and playing at Sea Island as is Austin Smotherman, a two-time winner in the fall who is at No. 50. Outside the top 50 but within range are 19-year-old Blades Brown (54) and Ben James, the No. 1 player from PGA Tour University with two runner-up finishes in the fall.
 RSM Classic 2026: Odds, favorites for Sea Island 
 It’s not Jackson Koivun. It’s not Michael Brennan. The name listed as the favorite for this week’s RSM Classic might surprise you. 
 Steve Coulter , 
 Steve Coulter , 
 2024 RSM Classic champ Maverick McNealy is No. 51 in the OWGR and playing this week. He said he hadn’t really thought about being on the top-50 cutoff when asked if there was more pressure this week with thoughts of Augusta National in his head.
 “It would be nice to get that invite in my Christmas stocking, but that said, if I do what I need to do with my ball-striking and my putting, I’d like to think I’ll be at the Masters,” he told reporters on Tuesday.
